topic.subject: science
topic.title: Wastewater story
topic.scope: sewage, treatment plants, sanitation, better housekeeping, open defecation and disease

misconceptions.statement: Sewage only consists of toilet waste and nothing else.
misconceptions.why: Students associate the word sewage primarily with human excreta.
misconceptions.fix: Sewage is a complex mixture containing suspended solids, organic and inorganic impurities, nutrients, and disease-causing microbes from homes, industries, and hospitals.

probe.question: Is rainwater that runs down the street during a heavy storm considered sewage?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because it doesn't come from a toilet.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its most common everyday example
misconceptions.source_hint: HBCSE research on water and environment

misconceptions.statement: Sewage and sewerage mean the same thing.
misconceptions.why: The words sound very similar and are used interchangeably in casual conversation.
misconceptions.fix: Sewage is the wastewater itself, while sewerage is the network of pipes (sewers) that carries the sewage.

probe.question: If a pipe in the city breaks, are we fixing the sewage or the sewerage?

misconceptions.root_belief: similar sounding words have the same meaning

misconceptions.statement: Bar screens remove germs and chemicals from the water.
misconceptions.why: Students often think any 'filter' or 'screen' makes water safe to drink.
misconceptions.fix: Bar screens only remove large physical objects like rags, sticks, cans, and plastic packets.

probe.question: Can a bar screen make wastewater safe from bacteria?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, it filters out all the bad things.

misconceptions.root_belief: one cleaning step removes all types of dirt

misconceptions.statement: All bacteria in wastewater are harmful and must be killed immediately.
misconceptions.why: Students are taught that bacteria cause diseases, so they assume all bacteria are 'bad'.
misconceptions.fix: In a treatment plant, aerobic bacteria are helpful because they consume human waste and other unwanted organic matter.

probe.question: Why do we pump air into the wastewater during treatment?
probe.wrong_answer: To kill the bacteria that cannot breathe air.

misconceptions.statement: It is okay to pour cooking oil down the sink because it is a liquid.
misconceptions.why: Students think liquids cannot block pipes because they flow easily.
misconceptions.fix: Fats and oils harden and block pipes; in open drains, they clog soil pores, reducing water filtration.

probe.question: What happens to liquid oil when it cools down in a sewer pipe?
probe.wrong_answer: It stays liquid and flows to the ocean.

misconceptions.statement: Clear water from a river or well is always safe for drinking.
misconceptions.why: Students rely on visual clarity as the only indicator of purity.
misconceptions.fix: Water may look clear but still contain disease-causing microorganisms and dissolved pollutants.

probe.question: If you see a clear stream in a forest, is it definitely safe to drink?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because you can see the bottom and there is no mud.

misconceptions.root_belief: what you cannot see does not exist

misconceptions.statement: Sludge is just useless mud that is thrown away.
misconceptions.why: Waste products are generally seen as having no value.
misconceptions.fix: Sludge is transferred to a separate tank where it is decomposed by anaerobic bacteria to produce biogas and dried for use as manure.

probe.question: What is the final use of the solid waste (sludge) collected in a clarifier?
probe.wrong_answer: It is buried in a landfill as trash.

misconceptions.statement: Fruit and vegetable peels are not pollutants because they are natural.
misconceptions.fix: Organic matter like food waste is a major pollutant in sewage because it rots and supports the growth of harmful microbes.

probe.question: Why are vegetable skins considered impurities in sewage?
probe.wrong_answer: They aren't; only chemicals from factories are real impurities.

misconceptions.statement: Chlorine is added to wastewater to make it clear.
misconceptions.why: Students observe that bleached or chlorinated water looks 'cleaner'.
misconceptions.fix: Chlorine or ozone are used as disinfectants to kill remaining harmful germs before water is discharged.

probe.question: What is the main purpose of adding chlorine to treated water?
probe.wrong_answer: To remove the brown color from the water.

misconceptions.root_belief: cleaning is only about visual appearance

misconceptions.statement: Septic tanks must be connected to the main city sewer line to work.
misconceptions.why: Students assume all toilets must lead to the same central system.
misconceptions.fix: Septic tanks are on-site sewage disposal systems where sewage is treated locally, suitable for places without a central sewerage system.

probe.question: Where does the waste go in a house with a septic tank but no city pipes?
probe.wrong_answer: It just stays in the toilet bowl.

misconceptions.root_belief: systems only work if connected to a central hub

misconceptions.statement: Flushing old medicines down the drain is safe because they are meant to cure people.
misconceptions.why: The positive association with 'medicine' masks its chemical nature.
misconceptions.fix: Medicines are chemicals that can kill the helpful microbes that naturally purify water in the treatment process.

probe.question: Why shouldn't we throw expired antibiotics into the sink?
probe.wrong_answer: Because they might make the water taste bitter.

misconceptions.root_belief: the purpose of an object defines its environmental impact

misconceptions.statement: You can only get water-borne diseases by drinking dirty water.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on the most direct route of infection.
misconceptions.fix: Diseases like cholera and polio can also spread through contaminated food or by touching contaminated surfaces/soil.

probe.question: Can a person get a water-borne disease if they only eat food handled with dirty hands?
probe.wrong_answer: No, you have to drink the water directly.

misconceptions.root_belief: one effect has only one specific cause
